title: Private bus drivers, conductors to receive ETF membership - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colobmbo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - Private bus drivers and conductors will be brought under the Employees' Trust Fund (ETF) scheme, marking a significant step toward extending social security benefits to employees engaged in non-government public transport services.

The Transport, Highways and Urban Development Ministry said an awareness programme on enrolling private bus crew members in the Employees' Trust Fund (ETF) scheme was held on July 21 at the Ministry Auditorium on the seventh floor of Sethsiripaya Phase II in Battaramulla.

The programme introduced participants to the role of the Employees' Trust Fund Board, the general and welfare benefits available to members, employer registration and contribution procedures, and the legal provisions governing membership under the Employees' Trust Fund Act No. 46 of 1980.

The initiative follows a decision by the ETF Board to extend membership to private sector employees engaged in public transport services, who were previously not covered under the scheme.

According to the Ministry, the programme is the first step in extending welfare benefits to employees in the non-government transport sector and will be implemented at both the central government and provincial council levels.

title: Ranil pushes for select committee to resolve 1.1 million pending court cases - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - Former President Ranil Wickremesinghe said he had proposed setting up a select committee to find ways and means to get rid of the backlog of cases.

"The government has claimed that the extension of the retirement age of judges is aimed at getting rid of the backlog of court cases. The Minister of Justice has said there are 1.1 million cases pending in courts. Therefore, I have told the Opposition Leader to hand over a proposal to the government calling for the setting up of a select committee to look into ways and means to resolve the large backlog of cases," Wickremesinghe told the media.

title: Sri Lanka among countries facing 10% US tariff under new forced labour policy - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Indian Express - Sri Lanka has been placed in the lower 10% tariff category under a new United States trade measure targeting imports linked to forced labour, according to the Office of the US Trade Representative (USTR).

The new tariffs, announced by the USTR on Thursday under the direction of US President Donald Trump, impose additional duties ranging from 10% to 12.5% on imports from 60 economies over what Washington described as inadequate measures to prevent goods made with forced labour from entering supply chains.

Sri Lanka is among 17 economies assigned the lower 10% tariff rate, together with India, the United Kingdom, Canada, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Mexico, Pakistan, Malaysia, Cambodia and several others.

According to the USTR, the 10% rate applies to economies that have banned imports produced with forced labour, committed to implementing such measures through reciprocal trade agreements, or already have partial restrictions in place.

The remaining economies investigated under the policy will face a higher 12.5% tariff, while products from the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Switzerland will also be subject to either a 10% or 12.5% tariff in addition to existing duties.

The new tariffs are scheduled to take effect from Friday.

USTR Ambassador Jamieson Greer said decades of international pressure had failed to eliminate forced labour from global supply chains and urged trading partners to adopt stronger import bans similar to those already enforced by the United States.

The investigations were launched in March under Section 301 of the US Trade Act of 1974, covering 60 economies. The USTR said it held discussions with more than 45 governments and reviewed over 1,600 public submissions before determining the final tariff rates.

Meanwhile, India, which had initially been considered for the higher 12.5% tariff, secured the lower 10% rate following what US officials described as constructive discussions with Washington on labour practices. The Trump administration also recently withdrew separate 25% tariffs imposed on India over its purchases of Russian oil.

title: CPA Australia Chief warns of ethical reckoning for accountants navigating automated financial systems - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Nishel Fernando

The global accounting profession is approaching a technological watershed, and professionals who fail to govern artificial intelligence with unwavering ethical standards risk systemic failures in corporate trust, warned CPA Australia President and Board Chair Prof. Dale Pinto.

Delivering the keynote address at the CMA Sri Lanka National Management Accounting Conference 2026 held in Colombo this week, Prof. Pinto asserted that while automation represents the future of finance, the sustainability of the industry hinges entirely on human judgment.

His remarks arrive at a precarious moment for the global financial sector, which has recently navigated high-profile corporate controversies involving audit oversights and the misapplication of artificial intelligence. Major global firms have faced immense regulatory scrutiny following revelations that personnel leveraged AI tools to circumvent internal ethics and compliance assessments, resulting in substantial financial penalties and severe reputational damage.

Furthermore, instances of algorithmic fabrication—where automated systems have generated fictitious regulatory reports and spurious data—have underscored the profound risks of relying on unverified technological outputs without robust human oversight.

Against this backdrop of industry-wide turbulence, Prof. Pinto argued that professional skepticism is no longer merely a best practice, but a critical line of defense. As algorithms increasingly handle predictive modeling and complex data processing, accountants must emerge as the ultimate guardians of corporate governance.

“Trust remains our most valuable asset, and in a world increasingly influenced by technology, the need for ethical leadership and human skills has never been greater,” he told the gathering of policymakers, business leaders and finance professionals.

He reminded the audience that algorithmic efficiency must never eclipse foundational principles, adding, “While technology may evolve rapidly, our ethical foundations must remain constant. Ethics is always on.”

The integration of artificial intelligence is fundamentally redefining the finance function, transitioning the accountant’s role from historical record-keeping to strategic, forward-looking stewardship. Prof. Pinto noted that AI systems are now seamlessly automating routine tasks such as transaction processing, variance analysis, and data extraction.

However, he firmly dispelled fears of mass professional displacement, insisting that the technology cannot replicate nuanced human analysis. “AI will not replace professional accountants; however, accountants who effectively harness AI may well replace those who do not,” he pointed out, advocating for a stance of responsible optimism.

Contextualizing these sweeping global shifts within the domestic landscape, Prof. Pinto observed that Sri Lanka stands at a vital economic crossroads where rigorous financial governance is imperative for sustained growth. Acknowledging the country’s remarkable resilience following recent macroeconomic challenges, he cited Sri Lanka’s highly educated talent pool and strategic geographic position as key drivers for long-term prosperity.

He stressed that local management accountants bear a direct responsibility to rebuild resilient institutions, enhance transparency, and attract sustainable foreign investment. Echoing calls from Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya for evidence-based decision-making, he emphasised that high-quality financial stewardship directly shapes national progress.

In mapping out the long-term trajectory of the profession, Prof. Pinto outlined five defining characteristics that will distinguish the next generation of finance leaders. He detailed that future accountants must be strategically focused on holistic value creation, technologically enabled to leverage automation, and data literate to transform raw analytics into actionable insights.

Furthermore, they must remain sustainability-minded and serve as trusted, ethical advisors who provide independent judgment. Addressing the contemporary adage that data is the new oil, he modified the premise to argue that information only holds competitive value when refined into insight and translated into strategic action. To successfully navigate periods of disruption, he advised organisations to cultivate agility, resilience, and foresight—capabilities that are deeply anchored by modern management accountants.

Ultimately, Prof. Pinto urged Sri Lankan finance leaders to move decisively beyond basic regulatory compliance. True stability and growth, he noted, will depend on integrating environmental and social sustainability considerations directly into core corporate strategies. The modern accountant must transform from a mere custodian of ledgers into an architect of organizational resilience.

«Our goal is evolving from reporting history to shaping the future, from measuring performance to creating value, and from managing numbers to leading transformation,» he concluded, challenging the profession to lead with both technological fluency and uncompromised integrity.

title: Sri Lanka targets US$300mn in cinnamon exports as Alba price hits record Rs. 7,500 - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Charithya Kumarasiri

Sri Lanka is targeting US$ 300 million in cinnamon export earnings this year as farm gate prices for premium Alba-grade cinnamon climbed to a record Rs. 7,500 per kilogram amid growing global demand.

Cinnamon Development Department Director General Janaka Lindara told Daily Mirror that Alba-grade cinnamon was fetching Rs. 7,500 per kilogram, while lower grades were selling at about Rs. 4,500. The prices reflect the amounts paid directly to farmers.

Cinnamon exports generated about US$108 million in the first five months of 2026, following record earnings in 2025, when cinnamon and related products brought in nearly Rs. 80 billion, or about US$ 260 million.

Sri Lanka produces about 25,000 metric tonnes of cinnamon annually from around 39,500 hectares cultivated across 19 districts. It exports cinnamon to about 92 countries.

The industry has accounted for between 1.7 percent and 2 percent of Sri Lanka’s total export earnings in recent years, as well as 23.4 percent of spice exports and about 8 percent of agricultural exports.

Mexico remains Sri Lanka’s largest cinnamon market, accounting for about 60 to 70 percent of exports, while the United States takes a further 11 to 15 percent. The industry is seeking to expand in higher-value markets in Europe, the Middle East and China, where demand for Ceylon cinnamon is growing.

The department aims to increase annual export earnings to US$ 500 million by 2030 and US$1 billion by 2035 under its strategic plan.

Lindara said meeting those targets would require a stronger regulatory framework through the proposed Cinnamon Development Bill, which is expected to support quality control and improvements throughout the production process.

The industry also sees potential to raise earnings through value-added products, including cinnamon oil and pharmaceutical products. Such products currently account for only about 5 percent of exports.

Increasing their share to between 10 and 15 percent could raise export earnings by as much as 50 percent without expanding the area under cultivation, according to the department.

Cinnamon-based agritourism is another largely untapped opportunity. Lindara said initiatives such as Cinnamon Trails could allow visitors to experience traditional cinnamon-processing methods and sample cinnamon-based food products.

However, the industry continues to face rising labour costs, a shortage of skilled cinnamon peelers, higher fertiliser and planting-material prices, outdated cultivation practices and inadequate infrastructure.

Difficulties in consistently meeting international food safety and hygiene standards have also restricted access to some premium markets. Competition from cassia, a cheaper substitute, remains a major threat, particularly as Sri Lanka continues to depend heavily on lower-value markets.

title: Tea exports fall in June despite stronger rupee earnings - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Tea export volumes declined for a second consecutive month in June, extending the industry’s weak first-half performance, although higher rupee-denominated export prices helped lift average earnings per kilogram amid continued pressure on global markets.

Tea exports totalled 21.25 million kilogrammes in June, down 2.02 million kilogrammes from the same month last year, with all product categories except bulk tea recording lower shipment volumes. The decline brought cumulative exports for the January-June period to 123.10 million kilogrammes, a year-on-year drop of 3.71 million kilogrammes.

Despite lower export volumes, the average free-on-board (FOB) value rose to Rs. 1,871.14 per kilogramme in June from Rs. 1,714.08 a year earlier, reflecting an increase of Rs. 157.06 per kilogramme. However, in U.S. dollar terms, the FOB value slipped to US$ 5.60 per kilogramme from US$ 5.72, highlighting the impact of currency movements.

For the first six months of the year, the average FOB value increased by Rs. 65.18 to Rs. 1,810.28 per kilogramme, while declining to US$ 5.70 per kilogramme from US$ 5.86 during the corresponding period of 2025.

Tea packets recorded the sharpest decline in June, with exports falling by more than 2.17 million kilogrammes year-on-year to 9.66 million kilogrammes. Tea bag exports also eased, while instant tea and green tea shipments recorded marginal declines. Bulk tea was the only category to register growth, increasing by about 307,000 kilogrammes from a year earlier.

During the January-June period, all export segments except instant tea posted lower shipment volumes compared with the same period last year. Instant tea exports rose by more than 427,000 kilogrammes, while tea packets accounted for the largest cumulative decline.

Türkiye remained Sri Lanka’s largest buyer of Ceylon Tea during the first half of 2026, importing 19.71 million kilogrammes, a 149 percent increase from a year earlier. Iraq ranked second despite a 28 percent decline in purchases, followed by Russia, which posted a marginal increase. Azerbaijan climbed to fourth place with a 72 percent increase in imports, while China overtook Libya to rank fifth.

title: Port City helipad among key aviation proposals - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July (Daily Mirror) - The Ministry of Defence has reviewed progress on measures to strengthen Sri Lanka's domestic aviation sector, with discussions including a proposal to establish a dedicated helicopter landing facility within Colombo Port City.

The progress review meeting was chaired by Defence Secretary Air Vice Marshal Sampath Thuyacontha (Retd.) and focused on balancing operational efficiency in domestic aviation with national security requirements.

Officials reviewed the implementation of key initiatives aimed at improving security clearance procedures, streamlining operational processes, and enhancing airspace management while ensuring air defence and national security standards are maintained.

A key topic of discussion was the proposed helicopter landing facility at Colombo Port City, which is expected to support future business travel, tourism, executive transport, and emergency response operations. The Defence Secretary instructed the relevant authorities to further evaluate the proposal in consultation with all stakeholders, citing its potential strategic importance to Sri Lanka's aviation infrastructure.

Representatives of the Aircraft Operators and Owners Association welcomed the Ministry's intervention, stating that nearly 90 percent of operational and regulatory issues that had remained unresolved for more than two decades have now been addressed through the Ministry's leadership and inter-agency cooperation.

The meeting was attended by representatives from the Sri Lanka Navy, Sri Lanka Air Force, Sri Lanka Police, Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka (CAASL), Airport and Aviation Services (Sri Lanka) Ltd. (AASL), Urban Development Authority (UDA), the Aircraft Operators and Owners Association, and senior Ministry of Defence officials.

title: Chinese Embassy seeks probe into Port City clash - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 23 (Daily Mirror) - The Chinese Embassy in Sri Lanka has urged Sri Lankan authorities to conduct a thorough investigation into a violent confrontation involving Chinese nationals at the Colombo Port City and establish the facts as soon as possible.

The Embassy said it was closely monitoring the incident and requested Sri Lankan police to ensure the personal safety and protect the lawful rights and interests of Chinese citizens in the country.

According to police, two Chinese nationals were injured during a clash between two groups of Chinese nationals at the Colombo Port City in the early hours of today. Another Chinese national was allegedly abducted during the incident.

The Colombo Harbour Police have launched an investigation into the incident.

Meanwhile, the Chinese Embassy advised Chinese citizens in Sri Lanka to enhance their safety awareness, remain vigilant, and report any emergency situations to the relevant authorities.

title: Mid-air 10-person brawl halts easyJet flight - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
BBC - A mid-air brawl involving around 10 passengers forced a Liverpool-bound easyJet plane to fly back to Tenerife, according to air traffic control.

The captain decided to return to the Spanish island about 30 minutes after departure "due to the danger" the fight "posed to the safety of the flight", the air traffic controller said.

Police met flight EZY3352 when it touched down at Tenerife South airport on Tuesday evening, per the crew's request.

The 186-passenger aircraft then continued to Liverpool.

The air traffic controller said in its statement, originally written in Spanish: "Our full support goes out to the crews and passengers who are increasingly having to endure these situations."

EasyJet said the plane "returned to the airport and was met by police due to a group of passengers behaving disruptively.

"The flight then continued to Liverpool."

The airline added: "Our cabin and ground crew are trained to assess all situations and to act quickly and appropriately to ensure that the safety of the flight and other customers is not compromised at any time.

"We take these incidents very seriously and do not tolerate disruptive behaviour towards our staff

"The safety and wellbeing of customers and crew is always our highest priority."

Air traffic control also said: "The crew of the flight from Tenerife South to Liverpool, after about 30 minutes of flight, informed us that they needed to return to the airport and requested police presence upon arrival.

"A group of about 10 passengers had started a fight on board, and the captain decided to return due to the danger it posed to the safety of the flight.

"We expedited their return as much as possible while coordinating with the airport for police presence.

"They landed and cleared runway 07 without incident."

title: Grade 5 Scholarship Examination 2026 to be held on August 9 - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 23 (Daily Mirror) - The Department of Examinations has announced that the Grade 5 Scholarship Examination 2026, conducted to select students for schools and award scholarships, will be held on Sunday, August 9, 2026.

The examination will be conducted at 2,723 centres islandwide.

Accordingly, Paper II will be held from 9.30 a.m. to 10.45 a.m., while Paper I will be conducted from 11.15 a.m. to 12.15 p.m.

The Department stated that the attendance registers of candidates who applied for the examination have been sent to the relevant Zonal Education Offices.

Candidates who need to amend their information can do so online from July 23 to August 3, 2026, by accessing the “Exam Information Centre” under “Our Services” on the official website www.doenets.lk or through http://onlineexams.gov.lk.

For further inquiries, candidates can contact the Department of Examinations via 011-2784208, 011-2784537, 011-2786616 or 011-2785413. The examination hotline is 1911.

title: Venue and dates for World Test Championship 2027 Final revealed - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
ICC - The Oval in London has been confirmed as the venue for next year's ICC World Test Championship Final, which will be played from Wednesday, 9 June to Sunday, 13 June.

The ICC announced last year that England had secured the hosting rights for the next three World Test Championship Finals — in 2027, 2029 and 2031 — with the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) responsible for selecting the venue for each edition.

This will be the second time that The Oval hosts the World Test Championship Final, having previously staged the showpiece in 2023, when Australia defeated India to lift the mace.

With less than a year to go, the current World Test Championship cycle is entering its business end, with nine teams still in the race to secure a place in the final.

Australia (87.50% points percentage), having won seven of their eight Tests, sit comfortably at the top of the standings, followed by defending champions South Africa (75%).

New Zealand (72.22%) remain within striking distance of the Proteas, while Bangladesh (58.33%) have moved firmly into contention after completing a 2-0 sweep of Pakistan in May.

Two-time finalists India are fifth with a points percentage of 48.15% after winning four of their nine Tests, narrowly ahead of Sri Lanka (41.67%).

England (24.36%), West Indies (15%) and Pakistan (8.33%) have significant ground to make up if they are to force their way into the World Test Championship final at the Oval.

The race to the World Test Championship Final will soon start to gather pace over July and August, with several crucial series set to shape the standings.

West Indies kick things off by hosting Pakistan in a two-Test series from 25 July, with both sides desperate for valuable points. Australia, meanwhile, will look to tighten their grip on top spot when they welcome Bangladesh for a two-match series starting on 13 August.

Attention then shifts to Asia as Sri Lanka and India lock horns in a two-Test series from 15 August, while Pakistan travel to England for a three-Test series spanning August and September.

Speaking on the announcement, ICC General Manager, Events & Operations, Gaurav Saxena, said: “The ICC World Test Championship Final has established itself as one of the most prestigious occasions in the global cricket calendar, bringing together the two best Test teams in the world after two years of sustained excellence and consistency.

“The 2027 World Test Championship Final will hold special significance as cricket celebrates 150 years of Test cricket. The Oval has played a proud role in the history of our sport and has hosted some of its most memorable moments. We look forward to working closely with the ECB to deliver another world-class event that celebrates the enduring legacy of Test cricket and creates lasting memories for fans around the world.”

Neil Snowball, ECB Managing Director, Competitions and Major Events, said: “We are honoured to be staging the next three ICC World Test Championship Finals in England and Wales, and we’re pleased to confirm that The Oval will play host again next year. The 2023 final at The Oval was a huge hit with broadcasters and fans, and I’ve no doubt that next year’s event will be extra special again.”

The first three editions of the ICC World Test Championship have each produced a different winner. New Zealand lifted the inaugural title in 2021, Australia claimed the mace in 2023 and South Africa ended their long wait for a major ICC trophy with a memorable triumph in 2025.

title: New train service from Colombo Fort to Thalaimannar Port begins tomorrow - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 23 (Daily Mirror) - Sri Lanka Railways will commence operations of a new train service between Colombo Fort and Thalaimannar Port from tomorrow (July 24).

Accordingly, Train No. 5003 will operate from Colombo Fort to Thalaimannar Port, while Train No. 5004 will operate from Thalaimannar Port to Colombo Fort.

The train will depart from Colombo Fort at 3.50 a.m. and will reach Thalaimannar Port at 10.44 a.m., while the return journey from Thalaimannar Port will commence at 4.10 a.m.

The service will operate through major railway stations including Gampaha, Polgahawela, Kurunegala, Galgamuwa, Anuradhapura, Madhu Road, Mannar and Pesalai.

Sri Lanka Railways stated that the train will not stop at the Anuradhapura New Town Railway Station until the ongoing renovation work at the station is completed.

The new service will include two air-conditioned first-class compartments with seat reservation facilities. Passengers can reserve seats through the railway reservation system or by visiting railway stations.

Sri Lanka Railways requested the media to inform the public regarding the commencement of the new train service.

title: Lanka Sathosa reduces prices of 11 essential food items - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 23 (Daily Mirror) - Lanka Sathosa has announced a reduction in the prices of 11 essential food items with effect from July 24, 2026.

The decision was taken following instructions issued by the Ministry of Trade, Commerce, Food Security and Cooperative Development, the state-owned retail chain said.

Accordingly, consumers will be able to purchase the selected essential items at reduced prices from all Lanka Sathosa outlets islandwide.

Lanka Sathosa said the price reductions are aimed at providing relief to consumers. The official announcement containing details of the revised prices has also been issued.

title: School second term to end on July 24 - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 23 (Daily Mirror) - The second school term for Sinhala and Tamil schools in government schools and government-approved private schools will end on Friday, July 24, 2026, the Education Ministry said.

Accordingly, the first phase of the third school term will commence on Monday, July 27, 2026.

Meanwhile, the second school term for Muslim schools will conclude on Friday, July 31, 2026.

The first phase of the third school term for Muslim schools will begin on Sunday, August 30, 2026, according to the announced school term schedule.
